builder.to_note: In Gmail, to: matches To, CC, and your sent BCC recipients. Combine to:me with negated cc:me to find emails sent directly to you.
builder.bcc_note: In incoming filters, bcc: usually only matches mail you sent. To catch received BCC mail, try deliveredto:you@gmail.com combined with negated to:me and cc:me.
builder.deliveredto_note: Matches the Delivered-To envelope header (useful for +aliases and forwarded mail; does not match Google Workspace domain aliases).
builder.exact_phrase_note: Matches the exact phrase inside quotes (Gmail ignores most punctuation except underscores and does not allow nested quotes).
builder.exact_word_note: Prevents Gmail stemming (e.g. +run won't match running). Note: plain words containing + without @ are auto-quoted.
builder.around_note: Finds emails where the two words appear within N words of each other. Do not combine OR inside AROUND.
builder.has_attachment_note: Matches messages with at least one attachment (including inline images).
builder.header_calendar_note: Official Gmail header operator supporting Google Calendar notification tokens (arbitrary third-party headers are not supported).
builder.category_note: Matches Gmail's automatic inbox tab. Because tabs are assigned by ML, category: works reliably in Search and may vary in incoming filters.
builder.label_note: Spaces inside label names are converted to hyphens (-) and nested slashes (/) are preserved. Search-only in standard Gmail filters.
builder.in_note: Standard Gmail searches omit Spam and Trash unless you include in:anywhere. Note: Gmail has no in:archive operator (for archive-only use -in:inbox -in:sent -in:drafts -in:spam -in:trash). Search-only.
builder.label_encryptedmail_note: Search-only: matches messages sent with Gmail Client-Side Encryption (Workspace).
builder.is_read_note: Search-only: matches messages you have already opened and read.
builder.is_unread_note: Search-only: matches messages you have not opened yet.
builder.is_starred_note: Search-only: matches messages you have starred (⭐) in Gmail.
builder.is_important_note: Search-only: matches messages Gmail or you marked as important (►).
builder.is_muted_note: Search-only: matches conversations you have muted in Gmail.
builder.date_after_note: Inclusive (starts at 00:00 of that day in your local timezone). Search-only: does not trigger on incoming mail.
builder.date_before_note: Exclusive (stops before 00:00 of that day — that day itself is NOT included). Search-only.

diagnostics.char_limit_warn: Approaching Gmail's ~1,500-character filter limit ({{count}} chars). Consider shortening or splitting if saving as an incoming filter.
diagnostics.char_limit_exceeded: Exceeds Gmail's ~1,469–1,500 character filter limit ({{count}} chars). Gmail may show "The specified search is too long" or silently fail to apply it — split into multiple filters.
diagnostics.or_negation_trap: OR + Exclude trap: placing a negated condition inside an OR group lets matching items bypass the exclusion. Move exclusions outside the OR group so they apply globally.
diagnostics.search_only_operators: Search-only operator(s) detected ({{operators}}): great for Gmail Search, but Gmail warns they usually won't match newly arriving emails in automatic filters (except rare chained-filter or POP3 setups).
diagnostics.caution_bcc: bcc: note: incoming emails hide other recipients' BCC headers, so this mainly matches emails you sent.
diagnostics.caution_category: category: note: Gmail assigns categories dynamically; ideal for Search, less predictable in incoming-mail filter rules.
diagnostics.wildcard_unsupported: Wildcard (*) detected: Gmail does NOT support * globs (e.g. *.docx). Use plain extensions (docx) or domain tokens (from:company.com) instead.
diagnostics.lowercase_or: Lowercase "or" detected inside a value: Gmail searches for the literal word "or" unless OR is uppercase.
diagnostics.unescaped_inner_quote: Extra double quote (") detected inside a quoted phrase: Gmail cannot escape quotes inside quotes and will close the phrase early.
diagnostics.negation_inside_operator: Inline negation (-term) inside a field value detected: consider adding a separate condition row with Exclude (NOT) checked instead.
diagnostics.around_with_or: AROUND does not accept OR or { } operands inside the expression. Create two separate AROUND conditions joined by OR instead.
diagnostics.conversation_view_negation: Thread-level negation note: with Gmail Conversation View enabled, a whole thread still appears if any other message in it avoids the exclusion.
diagnostics.deliveredto_me_unsupported: Gmail does not expand "me" in deliveredto: — enter your full email address or alias instead (e.g. you@gmail.com).
diagnostics.in_archive_unsupported: Gmail has no in:archive operator (archived mail simply lacks the Inbox label). Use -in:inbox -in:sent -in:drafts -in:spam -in:trash instead.
diagnostics.negated_group_caution: Negated compound group -(...) detected: works in Gmail Search, but may behave unpredictably in saved incoming filters. Prefer separate excluded conditions (-a -b) when possible.
diagnostics.double_negation: Double negation detected (an excluded condition inside an excluded group): Gmail does not support -(-term). Remove one of the exclusions.

help.title: Gmail Operator Reference
help.intro: Complete reference of Gmail search and filter operators, quirks, and account limits.

operators.desc: Matches the sender's email address or domain (e.g. from:company.com).
Matches ANY recipient (To, CC, and your sent BCC). Use to:me -cc:me for direct mail.
CC = carbon copy. BCC = blind copy (incoming mail hides BCC; use deliveredto:you@gmail.com -to:me -cc:me).
Matches envelope Delivered-To (+aliases, forwards). Does not match Workspace domain aliases.
Matches mailing list List-Id header (e.g. list:updates@service.io).
Searches within the email subject line.
Exact phrase in quotes or exact unstemmed word with +.
Proximity: word1 AROUND 5 word2 (wrap in quotes for strict order; no OR inside).
Attachments (incl. inline images) and filename/extension (pdf, docx — no * wildcards).
Matches embedded Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides links, or YouTube videos.
Official Calendar notification operator (e.g. rsvpAccepted, eventCancelled). Not for arbitrary custom headers.
Matches exact RFC 5322 Message-ID header.
Inbox tab: primary, social, promotions, updates, forums, reservations, purchases.
User labels (hyphenate spaces, e.g. label:My-Label), any label, or unlabeled mail (Search-only).
Client-side encrypted messages (Workspace, Search-only).
System location: inbox, sent, drafts, spam, trash, anywhere, snoozed, scheduled, chats (no in:archive; archived mail has no inbox label).

operators.op: is:read / unread / starred / important / muted / has:<star>
operators.desc: Message status or specific Superstar icon (Search-only).
Dates (YYYY/MM/DD or Unix epoch): after: is inclusive (00:00), before: is exclusive (Search-only).
Relative dates: 7d, 2m, 1y (Search-only).
Message size: 5M, 500K, or minimum size in bytes with size: (e.g. size:1048576).
Uppercase OR (or {a b}), exclusion -, and grouping parentheses (OR binds tighter than space AND).

tips: OR binds tighter than space (AND): mix OR and exclusions safely using groups, e.g. (label:work OR subject:urgent) -subject:Day.
Gmail does NOT support * wildcards (like *.docx) or regex. Use plain extensions (docx) or domains (from:example.com).
Gmail ignores most punctuation (! ? $ & # *) except underscores (_), and splits hyphenated numbers (01.2047-100 -> two numbers).
after: is inclusive (from 00:00 that day) while before: is exclusive (stops before 00:00 that day). Unix epoch timestamps work for sub-day precision.
Standard searches skip Spam and Trash unless you add in:anywhere.
Conversation View caveat: with threads enabled, -exclusions still match a thread if any other message in that thread does not match the exclusion.
Incoming filter rules run at arrival time: date, read/star, and label: operators are mainly for Search (Gmail warns they usually won't match new incoming mail).
Power tricks: label:^unsub finds bulk newsletters with Unsubscribe headers, and label:^smartlabel_receipt finds receipts.
Account limits: keep each filter under ~1,469–1,500 chars (1,000 filters max, 500 labels, 20 forwarding filters per account).

guide.title: How to apply your filter in Gmail
guide.intro: Once you have built your query with this tool, follow these steps to turn it into a permanent automatic rule inside Gmail.
guide.step1_desc: Click the [Copy] button in the «Generated search» card on this page. The query is now in your clipboard.
guide.step2_desc: Go to gmail.com in your browser and sign in if you haven't already.
guide.step3_title: Click the search bar at the top
guide.step3_desc: Gmail has a wide search bar at the top of the page (it says «Search mail»). Click anywhere on it.
guide.step4_desc: Press Ctrl+V (Windows / Linux) or Cmd+V (Mac) to paste. You will see the query appear in the search bar.
guide.step5_title: Click the Search options icon at the right end of the search bar
guide.step5_desc: Look carefully at the right edge of the search bar — there is an icon represented by three horizontal lines with sliders (Search options). Click it to open the advanced options panel.
guide.step5_tip: This is the step most people miss! The icon is subtle and sits right at the edge. In older Gmail versions it might be a small arrow ▼, but now it's usually this settings icon.
guide.step6_desc: A panel will open showing the search details. At the bottom of this panel, click the button that says «Create filter with this search».
guide.step7_title: Choose what Gmail should do automatically
guide.step7_desc: Tick one or more actions — archive, apply a label, mark as read, delete, forward... then click [Create filter] to confirm.
guide.done: Done! Gmail will now apply this rule automatically to every new matching email — no extra work needed.

privacy.p_2_1: Gmail Filter Builder is a tool designed under the "Privacy by Design" principle. By default, the application runs locally in your browser (client-side) and does not collect, store, or transmit to our servers any information about your emails, searches, generated filters, or personal usage data.

privacy.li_2_1: Technical connection data: When visiting the website, our infrastructure provider (GitHub Pages) may temporarily log your IP address and browser User-Agent for security purposes, DDoS attack prevention, and network performance.
privacy.li_2_2: Donations / Payments: If you choose to make a voluntary contribution to support the project via the donation system, the payment will be processed entirely by third-party platforms (Lemon Squeezy or GitHub Sponsors). We do not collect or have access to your bank or credit card data at any time.
privacy.p_3_1: To provide the service and enable development support features, we share strictly technical data or delegate processing to the following providers, with whom the mandatory Data Processing Agreement (DPA) exists:
privacy.li_3_1: Microsoft Corporation (GitHub Pages): Provides web hosting. Their servers may be located in the United States, operating under Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF).
privacy.li_3_2: Lemon Squeezy, LLC: Acts as the Merchant of Record for processing voluntary payments. If you donate via card, Apple Pay, or PayPal, Lemon Squeezy will collect your email and billing info under their own privacy policies, acting as the data controller for that payment.
privacy.p_4_1: We explicitly inform you that this website DOES NOT use generative Artificial Intelligence engines or automated decision-making systems in its filter creation functions. All generated code is based on deterministic programming logic.
privacy.p_5_1: You have the right to obtain confirmation on whether we are treating your personal data. Not having registered user databases, the exercise of rights is inherently limited to the technical nature of the website, but at any time you may exercise your rights of Access, Rectification, Erasure, Restriction, Portability, and Objection by sending an email to the contact address specified in the Centralized Legal Notice.
privacy.p_5_2: Likewise, if you consider that we have not treated your data properly, you have the right to file a claim with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) or your local authority.
